drivingQuestion: How can adding water render foul or flax-steeping water a permissible covering — how much would one have to pour?
outcomeNote: the clause 'until he adds water' is reassigned from foul/flax water to urine

segments.he: וְלֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה לֹא בַּמַּיִם הָרָעִים וְלֹא בְּמֵי הַמִּשְׁרָה עַד שֶׁיָּטִיל לְתוֹכָן מַיִם. וְכַמָּה מַיָּא רָמֵי וְאָזֵיל? אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר לֹא יִתְכַּסֶּה לֹא בְּמַיִם הָרָעִים וְלֹא בְּמֵי הַמִּשְׁרָה כְּלָל. וּמֵי רַגְלַיִם עַד שֶׁיָּטִיל לְתוֹכָן מַיִם, וְיִקְרָא.
segments.en: And we learned in the mishna: «And» one who needs to recite Shema «may not cover himself with either foul water or water» in which flax was «soaked until he pours» other «water into it.» The Gemara asks: «How much water does he continue to pour» in order to render them a permissible covering. If he is covering himself in water in which flax was soaked, it must be a considerable amount of water, requiring at least an equally considerable amount of water to neutralize it. «Rather, this is what it says: One may neither cover himself with foul water nor water» in which flax was «soaked at all; and urine,» which is considered repugnant, «until he adds» clean «water to it, and» only then «he may» recite Shema.

moves.summary: the mishna: not in foul water nor flax water until he adds water
moves.about: the mishna's clause: he may not cover himself in foul water or flax-steeping water until he adds water to it

moves.summary: how much water could he keep pouring to neutralize such water?
moves.about: how much water could he keep pouring into flax-steeping water to neutralize it — the clause as read is impracticable

moves.summary: rather the mishna means: never in those; and urine — until he adds water, then recites
moves.about: the mishna means: foul water and flax water are never a covering; and urine — until he adds water, then he recites
